title: Peer trigger request correlation rule
memory_recovered: A peer trigger request, a scheduling mutation, and a peer execution are three distinct provenance events. A later peer run does not satisfy an earlier pending request unless retained evidence explicitly correlates the request identifier to that run or records an authorized supersession.

sources.observation: The ledger contains pending requests with execution_claimed=false and preserves failed or unattempted direct-trigger evidence.
The project forbids claims of peer execution without evidence.
Continuity work requires immutable provenance and forbids reconstruction of unverified history.
Subsequent team artifacts and commits exist after older trigger requests, but commit existence alone does not identify which request caused a run.

observed: Pending trigger requests remain recorded with execution_claimed=false.
Repository work continued after those requests were created.
No immutable correlation identifier linking the pending requests to a particular peer run was found in the inspected canonical trigger ledger.
inferred: Temporal ordering alone is insufficient to prove causation or request satisfaction.
Treating any later run as satisfying any earlier request would collapse provenance and permit false peer-execution claims.
proposed: A trigger request may transition from pending only when a correlation record names request_id, target_team, trigger mechanism, immutable execution or run evidence, observed outcome, and correlation method.
Scheduling mutation evidence proves only that a schedule mutation was accepted; it does not prove execution.
When one run could plausibly answer multiple requests, each request must be individually correlated, explicitly superseded, or remain pending.
superseded: A peer run occurring after a request automatically proves that the request was executed.
An accepted automation update is equivalent to peer execution evidence.
A new team artifact may be retroactively assigned to an earlier request based only on subject similarity.
unresolved: Which, if any, later runs correspond to the pending VST and ICW trigger requests in operations/TRIGGER_REQUESTS.json.
Whether the trigger ledger should gain a first-class correlated_execution object or use additive per-request evidence records.

correlation_contract.fail_closed_rule: Absent execution evidence or an explicit supersession record, preserve status=pending and execution_claimed=false.

excluded: raw automation payloads not already present in the repository

evidence_strength: repository-grounded rule; pending request-to-run correlations remain unresolved
falsification_route: Produce immutable evidence that a named pending request directly caused or was explicitly consumed by a named peer run. That request may then be correlated without weakening the general rule.
